scope: H-S only, 36 new CE runs (GC10/GX10 global-backbone CORAL/Mixup first, then C10/X10 TPP-backbone); no H, no SupCon arms, no new environments

registry.queue_order: global-backbone arms (GC10, GX10) for all cells, then TPP-backbone arms (C10, X10)

decision_rule.purpose: Same-protocol generic domain-generalization baselines for the ICAIIC 2027 manuscript

arms.GC10: global MLP pooling (capacity-matched ERM backbone, as G10) + CE + DomainBed CORAL (gamma 1.0) on the fused 256-d feature
arms.GX10: global MLP pooling + CE + DomainBed inter-domain Mixup (alpha 0.2) on amplitude and phase
arms.C10: TPP + CE + DomainBed CORAL (gamma 1.0) on the fused 256-d feature
arms.X10: TPP + CE + DomainBed inter-domain Mixup (alpha 0.2) on amplitude and phase

decision_rule.primary_question: Does TPP + multiview SupCon (HS11) exceed ERM (G10) and generic DG methods applied to the same plain backbone (GC10, GX10)?
decision_rule.secondary_question: Given the TPP representation, does multiview SupCon (HS11) exceed generic DG regularizers (C10, X10)?
decision_rule.paired_with: completed v2 G10/G11 and historical H-S T-CE (HS10) / T-SC (HS11) runs of the same target and seed
reported: per-arm environment means and equal-environment means
95% percentile bootstrap interval over the nine pairs (10,000 resamples, seed 20261105)
decision_rule.interpretation: descriptive; no configuration of the main method is changed on the basis of these results
decision_rule.caveat: Nine pairs share three development environments; intervals are descriptive, not tests of independent environments

superseded_v1.note: ﻿2026-11-05: v1 (two TPP-backbone arms C10/X10) was started at 14:01 and stopped during its first job after a design review: external DG baselines must also be applied to the plain capacity-matched global-pooling ERM backbone (G10) to benchmark the TPP+SupCon combination. Superseded by h_dg_baselines_20261105_v2 (four arms GC10/GX10/C10/X10, global-backbone arms first). No target data was scored in v1; the interrupted attempt is preserved.
